The company reported Q3 revenue growth of 12% to $12.9 billion and operating income up 37%, with an operating margin of 34.6%. While concerns about tech giants' $700 billion AI infrastructure spending persist, the article suggests the long-term AI opportunity remains bright. Investment suitability depends on risk tolerance, with recommendations ranging from dividend-focused alternatives for cautious investors to quality AI players like Nvidia and Amazon for moderate investors.

items.title: INVESTOR ALERT: Webull Corporation Investors with Substantial Losses May Seek to Lead Class Action Lawsuit Before December 7, 2026 Deadline, Robbins Geller Rudman & Dowd LLP Announces - BULL
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Webull Corporation (NASDAQ: BULL) alleging the company made false statements about its independence from China. The lawsuit claims Webull misrepresented its operations as primarily U.S.-based when in fact 62% of its workforce and core technical infrastructure are tied to mainland China. A U.S. House Select Committee investigation corroborated these findings, leading to a 19% stock price decline on October 7, 2026. Investors with substantial losses can seek lead plaintiff status before the December 7, 2026 deadline.

items.title: Greg Abel Has 12.5% of Berkshire Hathaway's Portfolio in 3 Consumer Stocks. Here's My Top Pick to Buy Now.
items.summary: Greg Abel, Berkshire Hathaway's new CEO, oversees a $350 billion+ stock portfolio that includes three consumer stocks comprising 12.5% of holdings: Coca-Cola, Kraft Heinz, and Kroger. The article recommends Coca-Cola as the top pick due to its strong brand, consistent dividend growth (64 consecutive years), and thriving business performance, while cautioning that Kraft Heinz remains a turnaround risk and Kroger faces competitive pressures.

items.title: Qualcomm Doesn't Look Cheap Next to Its AI Chip Peers. Here's Why.
items.summary: Qualcomm's focus on edge AI chips for consumer devices limits its growth potential compared to Nvidia and Broadcom, which target hyperscalers spending billions on cloud AI infrastructure. Despite healthy 6% revenue and 27% EPS growth projections, Qualcomm significantly lags peers' 61-80% growth rates. Trading at 26x forward earnings versus Nvidia's 15x and Broadcom's 22x, Qualcomm appears overvalued relative to its growth prospects.

items.title: ROSEN, NATIONAL INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages AST SpaceMobile, Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - ASTS
items.summary: A securities class action lawsuit has been filed against AST SpaceMobile, Inc. for allegedly making false and misleading statements regarding its capital requirements, liquidity position, competitive standing in the satellite D2C market, and user adoption rates. Investors who purchased ASTS securities between March 4, 2025 and July 15, 2026 may be eligible for compensation. The lead plaintiff deadline is November 13, 2026.

items.title: ROSEN, A LEADING NATIONAL FIRM, Encourages Baidu, Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - BIDU
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is reminding investors who purchased Baidu securities between November 18, 2025 and August 17, 2026 of the November 13, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline in an ongoing securities class action. The lawsuit alleges that Baidu made false statements about its AI business's ability to offset declines in its legacy online marketing business, resulting in materially misleading statements about the company's prospects.

items.title: Not Anthropic. Not AMD. Here's My Top AI Stock for 2027.
items.summary: The author argues Nvidia is the best AI stock pick for 2027, despite its modest 30% gain in 2026. With revenue growth of 106% and EPS growth of 128% in Q2, Nvidia's stock is undervalued at 30x current earnings but trades at only 15x forward earnings. If the company achieves its projected 70% revenue growth in 2027 and the market re-rates it to a 30x multiple, the stock could double.

items.title: INNVENTURE DEADLINE: ROSEN, TRUSTED INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages Innventure, Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - INV
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm announces a securities class action lawsuit against Innventure, Inc. (NASDAQ: INV) for allegedly making materially false and misleading statements regarding Accelsius Holdings LLC's transformative deal with DarkNX. The lawsuit claims defendants overstated revenue and cash flow targets for 2026 when no evidence existed that DarkNX was constructing or facilitating a large-scale AI data center. Investors who purchased securities between November 17, 2025 and August 13, 2026 may be eligible for compensation. The lead plaintiff deadline is October 27, 2026.

items.title: GODADDY DEADLINE: ROSEN, SKILLED INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages GoDaddy Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important October 20 Deadline in Securities Class Action – GDDY
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm announces a securities class action lawsuit against GoDaddy Inc. for allegedly making materially false and misleading statements regarding customer growth strategy and average order size. The lawsuit claims GoDaddy implemented a promotion focused on short-term contracts that contradicted its public statements, leading to decreased bookings and deceleration of bookings growth in Q4 and full year 2025. Investors who purchased GoDaddy stock between September 3, 2025 and February 24, 2026 may be eligible for compensation. The lead plaintiff deadline is October 20, 2026.

items.title: 1 Reason to Buy Carnival Stock (CCL) in October
items.summary: Carnival Corporation posted record Q3 2026 results with $8.4 billion in revenue and $1.9 billion in net income, with strong demand for cruise travel continuing despite economic concerns. The stock trades at a forward P/E ratio of 8.4, representing a 50% discount to the S&P 500, suggesting potential upside if current positive trends persist. CEO Josh Weinstein highlighted record booked occupancy and pricing for 2027.

items.summary: Bank of America raised its quarterly dividend by 14% to $0.32 per share ($1.28 annually), offering a 2.4% yield. An investor would need 781 shares (costing ~$41,211) to generate $1,000 in annual dividend income. Despite headwinds from softer Wall Street revenue and regulatory pressures, BAC remains a solid dividend payer with 13 consecutive years of dividend increases and potential upside as the stock trades 17.5% below its 52-week high.

items.title: Can CoreWeave Unseat Amazon Web Services as the Top Cloud Provider?
items.summary: CoreWeave is a rapidly growing AI-focused cloud provider expanding at 112% year-over-year, compared to AWS's 37% growth. However, AWS maintains a massive 20x size advantage with $42.2B in quarterly revenue versus CoreWeave's $2.1B. At current growth rates, it would take CoreWeave nearly seven years to match AWS's revenue. While CoreWeave presents significant upside potential if it achieves profitability comparable to AWS's 39% operating margin, it currently lacks profitability and faces execution risks.

items.summary: Rosen Law Firm announces a securities class action lawsuit against XTI Aerospace, Inc. for investors who purchased securities between April 15, 2026 and August 17, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that senior executives engaged in undisclosed activities that required Board review, raising doubts about disclosure controls and the company's ability to file timely earnings reports. The firm is seeking a lead plaintiff by the October 27, 2026 deadline.

items.title: Is SoundHound AI a Buy After the LivePerson Deal?
items.summary: SoundHound AI has significantly expanded its enterprise opportunity through the acquisition of LivePerson. The key question for investors is whether the company can successfully convert this larger customer base into cross-selling opportunities, higher recurring revenue, and improved financial performance before mounting losses, declining legacy revenue, and shareholder dilution undermine the investment thesis.

items.title: Why ExxonMobil's Venezuela Warning Could Matter for Energy Investors Right Now
items.summary: ExxonMobil CEO Darren Woods initially called Venezuela 'uninvestable,' but the company is now reportedly in talks to invest in Venezuelan oilfields. However, Venezuela's production capacity remains severely constrained at 1.2 million barrels per day versus its historical peak of 3.5 million, meaning any investment there won't materially impact global oil prices in the near term. For ExxonMobil investors, Venezuela represents a potential bonus rather than a core growth driver, with the company's primary growth engines being its operations in Guyana and the Permian Basin.

items.title: NASDAQ: DUOL: Kessler Topaz Meltzer & Check, LLP Announces the Filing of a Securities Fraud Class Action Lawsuit Against Duolingo, Inc.
items.summary: A securities fraud class action lawsuit has been filed against Duolingo, Inc. for investors who purchased stock between May 2, 2025 and February 26, 2026. The lawsuit alleges material misstatements regarding monetization strategies and user friction that negatively impacted daily active user (DAU) growth. Duolingo's stock declined significantly following disappointing Q3 results (DAU growth fell to 36% from 49%), a CFO resignation, and weak Q4 guidance showing only 20% DAU growth for 2026.

items.title: Warren Buffett Held Wells Fargo Stock for More Than 30 Years Before Selling It. Here's the Lesson for Bank Stocks.
items.summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway held Wells Fargo stock for nearly 30 years starting in 1989, but exited the position in 2022 following the bank's 2016 phony accounts scandal. While CEO Charlie Scharf successfully turned the bank around with operational improvements and regulatory compliance, Buffett had already sold due to frustration with the board and uncertainty about the turnaround timeline. The case illustrates the importance of reputation in banking and the challenge of identifying viable long-term turnaround opportunities.

items.title: Sundar Pichai Reported Alphabet's Cloud Revenue Grew 82% to $24.8 Billion Last Quarter, With the Gemini App Reaching 950 Million Monthly Users. Is Google Cloud Becoming a Bigger Growth Driver Than Search?
items.summary: Alphabet's Google Cloud revenue surged 82% to $24.8 billion in Q2, significantly outpacing search revenue growth of 17%. With 950 million Gemini app users and a $514 billion revenue backlog, Google Cloud is emerging as a primary growth driver for Alphabet's AI-focused future, though search still accounts for over half of total revenue.

items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is seeking lead plaintiffs for a securities class action lawsuit against AppLovin Corporation (NASDAQ: APP) on behalf of investors who purchased securities between February 12, 2026 and August 5, 2026. items.title: INV INVESTOR ALERT: Innventure, Inc. Investors with Substantial Losses Have Opportunity to Lead the INNVENTURE Securities Fraud Class Action - HBSS
items.summary: Innventure, Inc. (NASDAQ: INV) faces a securities class action lawsuit after its stock price crashed 55% on August 14, 2026, following the company's removal of the DarkNX project from its 2026 forecast and suspension of revenue guidance. Forensic research firm Morpheus Research published a report claiming the 300MW data center project with DarkNX was non-existent, with former executives allegedly using 'false information' and 'pure fiction' for revenue projections. The company later confirmed the deployment site was no longer available, leading to a 74% stock decline between May 27 and August 14, 2026.

items.title: Netflix Is Reportedly Cutting 5% of Its Staff. Its 2022 Layoffs Came Days After the Stock Bottomed.
items.summary: Netflix is reportedly planning to cut around 5% of its ~16,000-person workforce (approximately 800 jobs) as early as next week. The layoffs aim to align non-content spending growth with slowing revenue growth. Unlike the 2022 layoffs that coincided with a stock bottom, the current situation differs: Netflix maintains double-digit revenue growth and a 33.4% operating margin, suggesting this is a margin optimization move rather than a defensive measure. The stock trades at 19x forward earnings, with revenue growth cooling from 18% to 13% year-over-year.

The law firm is offering free case evaluations to affected customers.

items.title: Buy, Sell, or Hold Delta Air Lines Stock After Q3 Earnings?
items.summary: Delta Air Lines reported disappointing Q3 results, missing earnings and revenue expectations despite record revenue and strong travel demand. Surging fuel costs (up 62% YoY to $4.14B) pressured profitability, prompting management to slash full-year EPS guidance from $6.50-$7.50 to $5.10-$5.60. The airline expects to absorb approximately $6 billion in additional fuel costs this year, highlighting industry-wide challenges.

items.title: DAL Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates as Higher Fuel Costs Hurt Margins
items.summary: Delta Air Lines reported Q3 2026 earnings of $1.72 per share, missing estimates by 4.44% as fuel costs surged 62%. While adjusted revenues climbed 16% to $17.59 billion driven by strong passenger demand and premium sales, the company cut its full-year 2026 EPS outlook to $5.10-$5.60 from $6.50-$7.50 due to elevated fuel prices and rising non-fuel expenses.

items.title: Cerebras Systems vs. IonQ: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares two specialized hardware companies: Cerebras Systems, which builds AI-accelerating wafer-scale processors and recently achieved profitability with $510M revenue but faces competitive pressure from Nvidia; and IonQ, a quantum computing leader with 202% revenue growth to $130M but still unprofitable with $510M net losses. The author recommends IonQ for 2026 due to its diversified customer base, expanding backlog, and fewer near-term competitive concerns, despite both being speculative early-stage investments.

items.title: Prediction: A $5,000 Investment Split Between Nvidia and Broadcom Will Triple by 2028
items.summary: Nvidia and Broadcom are positioned for significant growth through 2028, with both companies forecasting substantial revenue increases driven by AI infrastructure demand. Broadcom expects AI semiconductor revenue to reach $230 billion by 2028, while Nvidia projects 70% annual revenue growth. Based on these growth trajectories and historical valuations, an equal investment in both stocks could potentially triple by 2028.

items.title: Nvidia and AMD Lead the AI Market. 1 Chip Stock Has Far Greater Upside.
items.summary: While AMD has outperformed Nvidia in 2026 with a 200% rise versus Nvidia's 30%, the article argues Nvidia offers greater future upside. AMD's valuation has become stretched with its forward P/E ratio surging, and despite strong data center growth of 107%, it lags Nvidia's 117% growth. Nvidia's upcoming Vera Rubin chip architecture and projected 70% revenue growth in 2027 position it as the better investment despite being the world's largest company.

items.title: J.B. Hunt Gears Up for Q3 Earnings: What's in Store for the Stock?
items.summary: J.B. Hunt Transport Services is set to report Q3 2026 earnings on October 15, facing headwinds from rising freight costs, wage inflation, and weakness in its Final Mile Services segment. With an Earnings ESP of -6.99% and a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell), the company is unlikely to beat consensus estimates. The Truckload and Integrated Capacity Solutions businesses also face margin pressures amid challenging market conditions.

items.title: Can Monaco's Expanding Footprint Drive Molson Coors' Revenues?
items.summary: Molson Coors (TAP) acquired Monaco Cocktails through Atomic Brands to expand in the ready-to-drink spirits category. Monaco's first full quarter showed sales and profits ahead of expectations, with presence in five states offering significant expansion potential. Both Monaco and Fever-Tree are on track to contribute 1-2% of TAP's net sales. TAP stock trades at a discount valuation (7.68X forward P/E vs. industry average 14.18X) but has underperformed its sector over six months.

items.title: GE Aerospace Down 15% in 3 Months: Is This a Buying Opportunity?
items.summary: GE Aerospace shares have declined 15% in three months, but strong commercial engine demand, robust Q2 2026 revenue growth of 27%, and raised free cash flow guidance to $8.9-$9.2 billion support a positive outlook. However, elevated valuation at 34.79X forward P/E (above industry average of 27.16X), rising debt levels of $19.2 billion, and surging costs present risks. The stock maintains a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating despite trading below its 50-day and 200-day moving averages.

items.title: PepsiCo Just Reported Earnings. Here's What Investors Need to Know.
items.summary: PepsiCo beat Q3 earnings expectations with 3.1% organic revenue growth and a 3.7% stock price increase, despite cutting full-year EPS guidance to 2.5%-3.5%. The company faces challenges in North America beverages and snacks due to GLP-1 drug impacts and consumer pushback, but international segments remain strong. With a 4.6% dividend yield and P/E of 15, the stock may appeal to defensive dividend investors seeking recovery potential.

items.title: SPCX to Acquire 800 MHz Spectrum for Superior Network: Buy the Stock?
items.summary: SpaceX has agreed to acquire Grain Management's 800 MHz spectrum portfolio to enhance Starlink Mobile's connectivity capabilities. The low-band spectrum will enable a hybrid satellite-terrestrial network, improving indoor coverage and reliability. Combined with previously acquired 2 GHz spectrum from EchoStar, this positions SpaceX to compete as a major U.S. wireless operator while expanding its AI infrastructure ambitions.

items.title: 3 Top-Ranked Stocks Breaking Records on AI-Related Demand
items.summary: Micron, NVIDIA, and Hewlett Packard Enterprise have all posted stellar quarterly earnings driven by robust AI-related demand. Micron reported record Q4 revenue of $54.2 billion with strong pricing tailwinds, NVIDIA saw data center revenue surge 117% year-over-year to $89 billion, and HPE achieved record quarterly revenue of $12.2 billion with accelerating growth. All three companies maintain Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) ratings with bullish earnings estimate revisions and positive near-term outlooks.

items.title: Starbucks Explores CMG Deal: Smart Move or Costly Gamble?
items.summary: Starbucks has reportedly consulted advisers about acquiring Chipotle Mexican Grill, according to a Financial Times report. While the deal could diversify Starbucks' business and leverage CEO Brian Niccol's prior experience at Chipotle, concerns exist about financing requirements, integration challenges, and potential distraction from the company's ongoing turnaround strategy. No deal has been confirmed.

items.title: Reasons to Hold Veeva Systems Stock in Your Portfolio for Now
items.summary: Veeva Systems (VEEV) delivered strong Q2 fiscal 2027 results, beating estimates and raising its full-year outlook, driven by expanding Vault CRM adoption with 12 of top 20 biopharmas committed and over 180 customers live. The company is advancing AI initiatives with Veeva Falcon attracting early adopters. However, market saturation in the life sciences CRM space and intensifying competition from traditional and AI-powered platforms could constrain future growth rates.

items.title: Viatris to Buy Pacira for $1.65B to Expand Non-Opioid Pain Portfolio
items.summary: Viatris (VTRS) has agreed to acquire Pacira BioSciences (PCRX) for $1.65 billion in cash at $36.50 per share, expected to close by end of 2026. The acquisition adds two marketed pain therapies (Exparel and Zilretta) generating $350.5 million in H1 2026 sales, plus a mid-stage gene therapy candidate (PCRX-201) for knee osteoarthritis. The deal is expected to be immediately accretive to Viatris' financial metrics and strengthen its non-opioid pain management portfolio.

items.title: EMCOR Stock Trades at a Premium: Should Investors Buy or Steer Clear?
items.summary: EMCOR Group (EME) reported strong first-half 2026 results with 19.7% revenue growth to $9.78 billion, driven by robust demand for data centers, AI infrastructure, and healthcare projects. The company raised full-year guidance and achieved record backlog of $17.14 billion. However, the stock trades at a premium valuation (21.46x forward P/E) compared to peers, and faces headwinds from inflation, labor shortages, and supply-chain disruptions.

items.title: BlackBerry Jumps 13.3% in a Week as QNX and Earnings Momentum Build
items.summary: BlackBerry (BB) surged 13.3% in a week following stronger-than-expected earnings, with QNX revenues jumping 27.3% to a record $80.3 million and adjusted EBITDA rising 41.5%. The company raised fiscal 2027 guidance across revenue, EBITDA, and operating cash flow. However, the stock trades at 8.0X EV/Sales versus its 5-year median of 3.8X, creating a higher execution bar. Secure Communications showed weakness with declining net retention at 91%, and the company faces contract-timing risks. BB holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating with strong Growth and Momentum scores but weak Value score.

items.title: PEP Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Margin Pressure and Growth Plans
items.summary: PepsiCo reduced its 2026 core EPS growth guidance to 2.5%-3.5% from 5%-7% due to rising input costs, weaker margins, and unfavorable product mix. While the company reported strong international growth (8% organic revenue increase) and showed signs of North American snack recovery, beverage segment weakness and expiring commodity hedges remain concerns. Management plans increased brand investments and distribution restructuring to address North American competitiveness.

items.title: Here's Why You Should Retain DaVita Stock in Your Portfolio for Now
items.summary: DaVita (DVA) has rallied 55.8% year-to-date, driven by strong Integrated Kidney Care (IKC) platform growth, improving treatment volumes, and technology investments. The company beat Q2 expectations by $40 million in adjusted operating income and raised full-year guidance. However, persistent headwinds include declining revenue per treatment due to commercial-mix pressure (estimated $70 million impact in 2027), elevated G&A costs limiting operating leverage, and limited acquisition opportunities in a consolidated market.

items.title: ONTO's $1.1 Billion Backlog: Can Growth Accelerate Into 2027?
items.summary: Onto Innovation (ONTO) is experiencing significant growth driven by AI infrastructure spending, with backlog more than doubling to $1.1B in Q2 2026. The company raised full-year revenue guidance and expects 80% growth in advanced packaging. However, it faces intensifying competition from larger rivals KLA and Applied Materials, who are also benefiting from the semiconductor equipment boom.

items.title: Here's What $10,000 Invested in JPMorgan Chase When Jamie Dimon Became CEO Is Worth Now
items.summary: JPMorgan Chase stock has significantly outperformed the S&P 500 under CEO Jamie Dimon's 20+ year tenure. A $10,000 investment made when Dimon became CEO in 2006 would be worth approximately $83,020 today (730% gain), compared to $62,420 for the S&P 500 (524% gain). Including dividends, JPMorgan's total return reaches 1,320%, turning the initial investment into $141,540. Dimon plans to remain CEO for several more years.

items.title: Can Rising IRST Demand Support Boeing's Defense Growth Outlook?
items.summary: Boeing secured a $42.2 million contract to produce IRST Block II sensor assemblies for the U.S. Navy and Royal Australian Air Force. The company is well-positioned to benefit from growing military demand for advanced infrared sensing technologies that provide passive detection capabilities. However, Boeing's stock carries a Sell rating with declining earnings estimates and trades at a discount to industry peers.

items.title: Prediction: 2 Stocks That Will Be Worth More Than Broadcom 5 Years From Now
items.summary: The article predicts that Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and Palantir Technologies will surpass Broadcom's $1.7 trillion valuation within five years. AMD needs approximately 70% growth, supported by its major OpenAI deal for GPU capacity. Palantir would need to roughly quadruple from its current $456 billion valuation, driven by exceptional commercial revenue growth of 149% year-over-year. Both stocks carry execution risks but are positioned to benefit from AI market expansion.

items.title: AI Crawlers Turned Away More Than Twice as Often, a Check to Run Before an AI Visibility Audit
items.summary: Zen Media released guidance on AI visibility audits for brands that rank on Google but go unnamed in AI answers. Data shows AI crawler access denials increased to 13.47% in Q3 2026, with search and user-triggered AI requests growing from 6.51% to 11.92% between Q2 and Q3. The company's audit measures brand visibility across Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and Grok, identifying gaps between SEO performance and AI answer inclusion.

items.title: Top Storage Stock to Buy With $500 Right Now
items.summary: Everpure (formerly Pure Storage) is recommended as a top storage stock pick, with AI-driven demand accelerating revenue growth to 38% year-over-year. The company's software-based flash storage approach delivers superior price performance, and a recent hyperscaler deal is expected to generate significant revenue from fiscal 2028 onward. Trading at a reasonable 1.16x PEG multiple, the stock carries volatility risk from potential flash price reversals.

items.title: If You're Worried About an AI Bubble, Here's the Tech Stock Portfolio I'd Build
items.summary: Despite concerns about an AI bubble with some stocks trading at extreme valuations, the article identifies three major tech companies as relatively safe AI investments: Nvidia with a P/E of 31 and strong revenue growth, Amazon leveraging AI through AWS with stable e-commerce backing, and Alphabet benefiting from AI in advertising and cloud services. All three maintain strong liquidity and profitability despite significant capital expenditure commitments.

items.title: Taiwan Construction Market Size, Trends, and Forecasts by Sector to 2030 (H1 2026) | AI, Semiconductor Plants, Renewables, and Transport Drive 3.9% Annual Growth
items.summary: Taiwan's construction industry is forecast to expand 3.6% in 2026 and average 3.9% annual growth through 2030, driven by investments in semiconductor manufacturing, AI infrastructure, renewable energy, and transport networks. TSMC's strong Q1 2026 performance and government budget allocations of TWD3.0 trillion support continued market momentum, with private-sector investment pledges of TWD2.6 trillion from 1,712 companies further strengthening the outlook.

items.title: Here's Where Palantir and 4 Other AI Software Stocks Could Be in 5 Years
items.summary: The article analyzes five AI software stocks divided into two camps: those proving AI revenue (Palantir, CrowdStrike) trading at steep valuations with limited room for error, and those offering faster growth at lower multiples (SoundHound, AppLovin, ServiceNow). Each company presents different risk-reward profiles over the next five years, with concerns ranging from valuation sustainability to market dependency.

items.title: Michael Burry Is Betting Against Artificial Intelligence (AI). Here's the Case for and Against, and the One Stock I'd Still Own.
items.summary: Michael Burry has increased his bearish bets against AI stocks, warning of a potential crash. While concerns exist about massive infrastructure spending and monetization challenges, the article presents a balanced view noting AI is still in early adoption stages with strong revenue growth potential. Amazon is highlighted as the recommended stock to own regardless of AI's future, given its diversified revenue streams beyond cloud computing.

items.summary: The Security and Safety Services industry faces margin pressures from rising costs and labor expenses, but benefits from strong demand for security solutions. Four stocks highlighted are Allegion, ADT, Alarm.com Holdings, and Ituran Location and Control. The industry ranks #210 out of 247 Zacks industries and has underperformed the S&P 500 by 49.2% over the past year, though valuations remain attractive at 11.91X forward P/E versus the broader market's 19.99X.

items.title: Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights: Microsoft, Dell, HP, Lenovo and Nvidia
items.summary: Microsoft expanded its partnership with Nvidia, launching AI-powered Surface Laptop Ultra ($2,599) and Surface RTX Spark Dev Box ($5,999) to enable on-device AI processing. While Microsoft's growth outlook remains strong with FY27 revenue projected at $390.2B (+17% YoY) and FY28 growth of 18%, the stock trades at a premium 27X forward earnings. Earnings estimate revisions have been largely flat, and MSFT received a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, deemed more suitable as a long-term holding than an aggressive near-term buy.

items.title: Nebius Group vs. SoundHound AI: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: Nebius Group and SoundHound AI represent different plays in the AI infrastructure boom. Nebius operates a specialized cloud platform for AI workloads with 350% revenue growth and demand exceeding supply, while SoundHound AI provides voice-enabled software with 99% revenue growth but faces profitability challenges and integration risks. The author recommends Nebius due to its stronger market position and less competitive landscape.

items.title: BigBear.ai vs. Nebius: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares two AI-focused tech stocks with opposite market approaches. BigBear.ai provides defense and government intelligence software but faces declining revenue (down 19% in 2025) and mounting losses ($294M net loss). Nebius Group operates AI cloud infrastructure with explosive 479% revenue growth in 2025 and positive net income of $82M, though it carries massive negative free cash flow due to capital-intensive GPU infrastructure spending. The author recommends Nebius as the better buy, citing its larger addressable market ($1 trillion GPU cloud opportunity), consistent profitability, and superior growth trajectory compared to BigBear.ai's struggling government contract model.

items.title: ROSEN, LEADING INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages Duolingo, Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - DUOL
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm has filed a class action lawsuit against Duolingo, Inc. on behalf of investors who purchased Class A common stock between May 2, 2025 and February 26, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that Duolingo made materially false statements regarding Daily Active User growth rates, failed to disclose that increased user friction from ads and subscription upsells was negatively impacting DAU growth, and concealed that AI-generated content was degrading product quality and user experience. The deadline to serve as lead plaintiff is December 7, 2026.

items.title: GDDY IMPORTANT DEADLINE: ROSEN, NATIONAL INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages GoDaddy Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important October 20 Deadline in Securities Class Action – GDDY

Investors who purchased stock during specified periods may be eligible for compensation, with an October 20, 2026 deadline to serve as lead plaintiff.

items.title: PepsiCo Maintains Food and Beverage Volume Growth. Here’s Why Earnings Are Under Pressure Anyway.
items.summary: PepsiCo beat Q3 earnings estimates and raised full-year revenue guidance, but cut profit guidance due to North American business struggles, higher operating costs, and margin compression. The company plans cost-cutting measures and selective price increases on snack brands to address headwinds from inflation and changing consumer preferences.

items.title: PepsiCo vs. Coca-Cola: Can PEP Stock Catch Up to KO After Its Q3 Earnings Beat?
items.summary: PepsiCo beat Q3 earnings expectations but lowered full-year guidance, citing North American weakness and margin pressures. Despite attractive valuation and higher dividend yield, PEP significantly underperformed Coca-Cola year-to-date. Coca-Cola's stronger growth outlook, improved margins, and premium valuation make it the more appealing near-term investment, while PepsiCo may need to demonstrate improved domestic demand and margin recovery before a sustained turnaround.

items.summary: Freeport-McMoRan (FCX) declined 1% on October 8, 2026, underperforming the S&P 500's 0.47% loss. The stock has fallen 5.73% over the past month, significantly lagging the sector. However, the company is expected to report strong Q3 earnings on October 27 with 46% EPS growth year-over-year, and full-year guidance shows 63.84% earnings growth. FCX currently holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) with a Forward P/E of 24.81, trading at a slight discount to its industry average.

items.title: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon Just Issued a Blunt Warning About Artificial Intelligence
items.summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon warned that cybersecurity risks have increased 10-fold following the release of Anthropic's advanced Claude Mythos AI model, which has capabilities including multi-step reasoning and the ability to penetrate advanced cybersecurity systems. While not in panic mode, Dimon emphasized the need to address these emerging AI-related threats seriously.

items.title: SpaceX's Google AI Pact Is Worth Up to $29 Billion, but Investors Shouldn't Bank on It
items.summary: Alphabet will pay SpaceX $920 million monthly for compute capacity in a deal potentially worth $29 billion over 32 months. SpaceX must prove competitive advantages in a less constrained market.

items.title: General Motors vs. Tesla: What Revenue Growth Trends Tell Investors About These Automotive Giants
items.summary: While General Motors maintains a larger absolute revenue scale ($48B vs $28.2B in Q2 2026), Tesla demonstrates significantly stronger growth momentum with 26% year-over-year revenue increase compared to GM's 2% growth. Tesla's EV dominance continues despite expired federal tax credits, while GM struggles with a 43% decline in EV sales and relies on hybrid and gas-powered vehicles alongside AI initiatives.

items.title: STZ Q2 Earnings Call Highlights Improving Demand and Outlook
items.summary: Constellation Brands (STZ) reaffirmed its fiscal 2027 EPS guidance of $11.20-$11.90 during its Q2 earnings call, citing improving September beer demand, stronger marketing execution, and healthier distributor inventories. The company beat earnings expectations ($3.74 vs. $3.62 consensus) and revenue estimates ($2.63B vs. $2.57B consensus). While Pacifico and Victoria showed strong growth (20% and mid-teens respectively), Modelo and Corona faced headwinds. Management projects second-half beer margins of 34.5%-35.5% amid higher marketing costs and seasonal weakness.

items.title: CVS Health Trades at a Discount to Industry: How to Play the Stock?
items.summary: CVS Health demonstrates attractive valuation and improving business performance, with Aetna's margin recovery gaining momentum and pharmacy segment showing strong prescription volume growth. The stock trades at a discount to peers and has outperformed its industry, though technical indicators suggest weaker momentum.

items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Innventure, Inc. (NASDAQ: INV) alleging securities fraud. The complaint claims the company made false statements about its subsidiary Accelsius's transformative deal with DarkNX, which allegedly lacked credible evidence of execution, and that revenue targets for 2026 were not reasonably plausible. Investors who purchased Innventure securities between November 17, 2025 and August 13, 2026 are encouraged to join the case.

items.title: Better Cloud AI Pick: CoreWeave or Nebius Group?
items.summary: CoreWeave and Nebius are competing AI cloud computing providers with impressive growth rates. items.title: Jabil's FY27 AI Revenue Surge Could Redefine Its Growth Story in 2027
items.summary: Jabil Inc. (JBL) reported strong Q4 fiscal 2026 results and projects AI revenues to surge 54% to $22.1 billion in fiscal 2027. However, execution risks remain as Jabil expands capacity globally to support larger customer programs.

items.title: Is Jabil a Buy After AI Growth as Valuation Stays Above Its Median?
items.summary: Jabil Inc. (JBL) projects fiscal 2027 revenues of $44.5 billion (+24% YoY) and core EPS of $17.55 (+34% YoY), driven by AI-related revenues surging 54% to $22.1 billion. items.title: Pfizer's Oncology Outlook: Key Drivers to Watch Ahead of Q3 Results

The company expects Q3 growth driven by newer drugs like Padcev, Lorbrena, and Braftovi-Mektovi, offset by declines in Ibrance and Adcetris. Pfizer is advancing the dual PD-1/VEGF inhibitor PF-08634404 across nine studies including two pivotal phase III trials. The stock trades at an attractive valuation with a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating.

items.title: Are You Looking for a Top Momentum Pick? Why Fortinet (FTNT) is a Great Choice

items.title: Can Willis Towers' Growth Momentum Continue Amid Soft Pricing?
items.summary: Willis Towers Watson (WTW) achieved 5% organic revenue growth in Q2 2026, driven by its Risk & Broking segment (7% growth) and specialization strategy. The company maintains mid-single-digit growth guidance for 2026, though sustaining this pace depends on continued new business wins and offsetting softer insurance pricing. Peers Brown & Brown faced headwinds with declining organic growth, while Arthur J. Gallagher demonstrated stronger positioning with 6% organic growth expectations.

items.title: AbbVie's Temab-A Gets Two FDA Breakthrough Therapy Tags in Cancer
items.summary: AbbVie announced that its investigational antibody-drug conjugate Temab-A (telisotuzumab adizutecan) has received two FDA Breakthrough Therapy designations for colorectal cancer and non-small cell lung cancer. The designations were based on data from the M21-404 study, and the company is evaluating Temab-A across multiple advanced solid tumors as part of its expanding oncology pipeline.

items.title: YUMC or CMG: Which Is the Better Value Stock Right Now?
items.summary: A comparison of two restaurant stocks shows Yum China Holdings (YUMC) as the superior value option compared to Chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG). YUMC has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) with improving earnings outlook and significantly better valuation metrics, including a forward P/E of 13.77 versus CMG's 26.88, and a Value grade of A versus CMG's D.

items.title: Applied Digital Has $36 Billion in Contracted Revenue. Is the Stock a Buy?
items.summary: Applied Digital has secured $36 billion in contracted AI data center revenue, but most capacity still needs to be built. The key question for investors is whether the company can convert these signed leases into profitable operating assets while managing construction progress, financing costs, and customer concentration risks.

items.title: Best Buy's Ads & Marketplace Expansion Opens New Growth Opportunities
items.summary: Best Buy is expanding its advertising and marketplace businesses to create additional profit streams and improve margins. Best Buy Ads targets 10% collections growth in fiscal 2027 on $900 million in prior-year collections, while Marketplace GMV outlook was raised to $1.3 billion after strong Q2 results. These initiatives contributed to a 60 basis point increase in domestic gross margin to 24%, and management raised fiscal 2027 adjusted operating income guidance to 4.4-4.5%.

items.title: Jensen Huang Has Dismissed AI "Doomsday Narratives," Saying, "Scaring People Is Unnecessary. It Is Irresponsible." Here's Why That Stance Matters for Nvidia's Growth Story.
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang dismissed concerns about AI risks and development slowdowns, stating that fears are overblown and that 2030 will not be 'the end of the world.' While some AI leaders like Anthropic's Dario Amodei have called for slower development, Huang argues that safe deployment of AI products directly benefits Nvidia's long-term value. Despite initial stock declines following AI safety warnings, Nvidia has recovered and hit new highs, with Wall Street expecting 91% year-over-year revenue growth.

items.title: Can Microsoft's Big AI Capex Translate Into Sustainable Returns Ahead?
items.summary: Microsoft's massive AI infrastructure spending is supported by $678 billion in commercial remaining performance obligations, with Azure revenues exceeding $100 billion. The company expects double-digit growth in fiscal 2027 despite capex exceeding $50 billion quarterly. Amazon and Alphabet are pursuing similarly aggressive AI buildouts with strong cloud revenue growth and substantial backlogs, though Alphabet's free cash flow turned negative.

items.title: Can Super Micro Computer Sustain Its AI Capex Momentum in 2027?
items.summary: Super Micro Computer (SMCI) reported fiscal 2026 revenues of $39.1 billion, up 78% year-over-year, with over $60 billion in new orders received in Q4. The company is capitalizing on the AI infrastructure boom through early availability of systems supporting NVIDIA and AMD platforms, expanding enterprise customers (31% of sales, up 39% YoY), and developing liquid-cooling solutions for high-performance AI systems. SMCI trades at a valuation discount (0.42X P/S vs. industry 3.03X) and holds a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) rating.

items.title: Prediction: Johnson & Johnson Will Be a Faster-Growing Company by 2030 Than Most Investors Expect
items.summary: Johnson & Johnson is positioned for faster growth by 2030 following its separation from its slower-growing consumer health division. The company can now focus investments on its faster-growing biopharma and medtech segments. Key growth drivers include recent drug approvals like ICOTYDE and the FDA-cleared Ottava robotic surgery system, which operates in a market with significant expansion potential. Despite challenges from government price negotiations and talc-related lawsuits, J&J's diversified portfolio and strong dividend history make it an attractive long-term investment.

items.title: APP Investors: AppLovin Corporation Shares Declined By $82.13 On August 6, 2026 -- Contact Kirby McInerney LLP to Discuss Your Rights

items.title: Can L3Harris' Propulsion Capacity Expansion Unlock New Growth?

The company's Aerojet Rocketdyne segment saw 10% revenue growth in fiscal 2025, driven by increased missile production volumes. LHX plans to expand its Camden, Arkansas facility and is investing in manufacturing infrastructure to support higher output. The company is trading at a discount relative to its industry peers.

items.title: Here's Why You Should Consider Investing in Nordson Stock Now
items.summary: Nordson Corporation (NDSN) is experiencing strong performance across its business segments with 31% organic sales growth in Advanced Technology and 11% in Medical and Fluid Solutions. items.title: PepsiCo Q3 Earnings & Revenues Beat Estimates on International Growth

items.title: Is Nvidia, at Bargain Levels Right Now, a Buy? Here Are the Bull and Bear Cases.

items.title: Better Cloud Investment: Amazon or Nebius Group?

Orbital data centers are unlikely to replace terrestrial data centers in the near term.

items.title: Not Nvidia. Not Micron. If I Could Buy and Hold Only 1 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Chip Stock Through 2030, It Would be This One.
items.summary: While Nvidia and Micron dominate AI chip headlines, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) is positioned as the superior long-term AI infrastructure play. TSMC controls ~73% of the foundry market and ~90% of advanced-node capacity, making it the critical bottleneck in AI chip production. With AI-accelerator revenue expected to compound at 50%+ through 2030, strong financial growth (36% YoY revenue growth in 2025), expanding margins, and a forward P/E of 28, TSMC offers better value than chip designers while maintaining a durable competitive moat.

items.summary: Vietnam's veterinary vaccine import market is expanding due to growing livestock and aquaculture sectors, with imports valued at US$172 million in 2024. The market remains highly dependent on imported vaccines, particularly from the US (34.6%), China (12.8%), and Netherlands (8.7%). International companies like Zoetis, MSD Animal Health, and Boehringer Ingelheim maintain strong positions, while foreign investment opportunities are emerging through joint ventures and local manufacturing partnerships.

items.title: President Donald Trump's Investment Team Sold Up to $25 Million in 2 Foundational AI Stocks in July
items.summary: President Trump's investment team completed 1,156 trades in July 2026, including sales of up to $25 million each in Amazon and Microsoft. Despite both companies' strong AI performance—AWS reported 37% YoY revenue growth and Azure grew 43%—the sales likely reflect profit-taking and concerns about overvalued AI stocks amid historically high market valuations.

items.title: Pfizer Is Down 34% Over the Last 5 Years. Here's Why Its 6% Dividend Yield Might Finally Be Worth the Risk.
items.summary: Pfizer's stock has declined 34% over five years due to falling coronavirus product demand and patent expirations on key drugs. However, the company's recent strategic acquisitions (Seagen, Metsera, Biohaven), regulatory approvals, and cost restructuring efforts are showing positive results. With management confident in maintaining its 6% dividend yield and the stock trading at a reasonable 9.6x forward earnings, the pharmaceutical giant may now present a compelling opportunity for dividend investors.

items.summary: GE Aerospace and SpaceX represent contrasting investment profiles in the aerospace sector. The article recommends GE Aerospace as the more prudent long-term investment due to its established market position, profitability, and government support, while cautioning that SpaceX remains a high-risk, high-growth speculation.

items.title: Nike (NKE) Q1 Earnings Surpass Estimates
items.summary: Nike reported Q3 2026 earnings of $0.48 per share, beating consensus estimates of $0.43, but revenues of $11.21 billion missed expectations by 1.65%. Despite the EPS beat, the stock has underperformed significantly, down 44.4% year-to-date versus the S&P 500's 11.8% gain. The company received a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) rating due to unfavorable estimate revision trends, with the Shoes and Retail Apparel industry ranking in the bottom 15% of sectors.

items.title: Micron Earnings: AI-Driven Memory Cycle Remains Strong
items.summary: Micron Technology reported record Q4 revenue of $54.2 billion, up 31% sequentially and 379% year-over-year, with adjusted EPS of $33.42 beating consensus estimates. Strong pricing in both DRAM and NAND segments, combined with robust visibility through 2027 and strategic customer agreements, indicate the AI-driven memory cycle remains powerful with continued growth expected through fiscal 2027.

items.title: XTIA 投資者提醒：Rosen Law Firm 提醒 XTI Aerospace, Inc. 投資者，證券集體訴訟首席原告截止日期為 2026 年 10 月 27 日
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm announced a securities class action lawsuit against XTI Aerospace, Inc. (NASDAQ: XTIA) on behalf of investors who purchased securities between April 15, 2026 and August 17, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that company executives engaged in undisclosed activities and that the company made materially false and misleading statements regarding its disclosure controls, procedures, and ability to timely file earnings reports. The deadline to apply for lead plaintiff status is October 27, 2026.

items.title: Buy Micron Stock After AI Memory Demand Fuels Record Q4 Results?
items.summary: Micron Technology reported record Q4 earnings of $33.42 per share and revenue of $54.23 billion, driven by surging demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and data-center storage. The company projects Q1 2027 revenue of $61.5 billion with continued strong growth, while trading at an attractive 7X forward earnings multiple despite its 250% year-to-date rally.

items.title: ASML vs. SK Hynix: What Revenue Trends Reveal to Investors About These Artificial Intelligence Companies
items.summary: SK Hynix and ASML are both benefiting from AI demand, but their revenue trajectories differ significantly. ASML shows steady, gradual quarterly growth due to long manufacturing timelines for EUV lithography equipment, while SK Hynix demonstrates rapid acceleration in memory chip sales driven by surging demand and rising memory prices. SK Hynix's Q2 2026 revenue reached $52.6 billion compared to ASML's $10.8 billion, highlighting divergent growth patterns in the semiconductor supply chain.

items.title: Applied Materials vs. AMD: Which AI Semiconductor Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: Applied Materials and AMD offer different exposure to AI semiconductor demand. Applied Materials supplies chip manufacturing equipment with a lower valuation (P/E 23.4x) and improving growth trajectory, while AMD designs processors with faster 2025 revenue growth (34.3%) but faces potential shareholder dilution from OpenAI and Meta warrants covering ~20% of shares outstanding. The author recommends Applied Materials as the better buy, though both stocks have merit for long-term diversified portfolios.

items.title: Are Oils-Energy Stocks Lagging  Chevron (CVX) This Year?
items.summary: Chevron (CVX) has gained 34% year-to-date, outperforming the Oils-Energy sector average of 27.8%, with a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) and improving earnings outlook. Kinetik Holdings Inc. (KNTK) has returned 39.3% year-to-date with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) and significantly increased earnings estimates.

items.title: Arm vs. ASML: Which Semiconductor Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares Arm Holdings and ASML as semiconductor investment options. Arm licenses chip designs with a high-margin business model (93.88% gross margin, P/E 297.15), while ASML manufactures essential lithography equipment with a monopoly position (52.73% gross margin, P/E 56.35). The author recommends ASML due to its irreplaceable role as the sole provider of extreme ultraviolet lithography machines critical to advanced chip production, despite Arm's consistent growth in mobile and data center segments.

items.title: Arm vs. Credo Technology Group: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: Arm and Credo Technology Group represent two different plays on AI infrastructure growth. Arm provides processor architecture for billions of devices with a durable royalty model and 22.8% revenue growth, while Credo offers high-speed connectivity solutions with explosive 205.7% revenue growth but faces customer concentration risk. The author recommends Credo for growth-focused investors despite higher risk, while Arm suits those seeking consistency.

items.title: Warren Buffett Just Stepped Down as Berkshire's Chairman After Delivering a 19.7% Annual Return Over 61 Years. Should Shareholders Be Concerned?
items.summary: Warren Buffett, 96, has stepped down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway after 61 years of leadership, achieving 19.7% annualized returns. His son Howard Buffett has taken over as chairman while Greg Abel continues as CEO. The article argues shareholders should not be concerned as the transition was carefully planned and both successors were hand-selected and trained by Buffett to maintain the company's culture and values.

items.title: Micron's Next Big AI Opportunity Could Have 2 Legs
items.summary: Micron Technology has identified a significant growth opportunity beyond data center AI infrastructure: physical AI applications including humanoid robots and autonomous vehicles. CEO Sanjay Mehrotra noted these devices require comparable memory and storage to data centers (200+ GB of DRAM), potentially creating demand for 'server-level memory in millions of machines' outside data centers. With fiscal 2026 revenue up 257% and strong guidance for fiscal 2027, this could extend Micron's growth cycle well beyond the current AI infrastructure build-out.

items.title: UPS Dips Below $94 and Has a 7% Dividend Yield: Time to Buy?
items.summary: UPS stock has fallen below $94, offering a 7% dividend yield that may attract income investors. However, the company faces significant headwinds including margin pressure from rising fuel costs, volume declines from the Amazon glide-down, and competition from Amazon's new supply chain services. With dividend costs of $5.4 billion against estimated free cash flow of $5.5 billion, there is minimal coverage for earnings deterioration, making this a risky entry point despite the attractive yield.

items.title: Amazon Inks $1B SNPS Deal to Power AWS Custom Chips: Should You Hold?
items.summary: Amazon signed a $1B+ multi-year IP agreement with Synopsys to accelerate custom chip design for AWS. AWS revenues grew 37% to $42.2B in Q2 with a $496B backlog, while Amazon's chips business surpassed $25B annual revenue run rate. However, Amazon raised 2026 capex to $220B, resulting in negative free cash flow and capacity constraints. The stock trades at a premium valuation with intensifying competition from Microsoft, Google, and Oracle in cloud infrastructure.

items.title: Vertiv Soars 49% YTD: Is This the Right Time to Buy the Stock?
items.summary: Vertiv (VRT) has outperformed the broader tech sector with a 48.9% year-to-date gain, driven by strong AI data center demand and a comprehensive power and cooling portfolio. Q2 sales rose 24% with Americas and APAC each growing 29%. The company reported an adjusted operating margin of 22.6%, up 410 basis points year-over-year, and raised full-year margin guidance to 23.3%-24.3%. For Q3 2026, Vertiv expects revenues of $3.65-$3.85 billion and adjusted EPS of $1.77-$1.83, though the stock is trading at a premium valuation.

items.title: Can Kroger's Digital Growth Offset Its Softer Fiscal 2026 Sales View?
items.summary: Kroger reported Q2 adjusted EPS growth of 4.8% but disappointed on sales, with identical sales excluding fuel rising only 0.2%. The company cut fiscal 2026 identical-sales guidance to 0.2%-0.8% from 1%-2%, citing pharmacy headwinds, logistics pressures, and deflation. However, e-commerce sales surged 20% and Precision Marketing profit grew 24%, providing profit-mix improvements despite top-line constraints.

items.title: Penguin Solutions' AI Backlog Grows: Is Future Sales Taking Shape?
items.summary: Penguin Solutions (PENG) enters Q4 FY26 with strong AI-driven backlog as customer demand outpaces sales. Integrated Memory revenues surged 111% YoY to $275M, and the company raised FY26 net sales growth outlook to 22%. However, PENG faces intensifying competition from Super Micro Computer and Dell Technologies, both building substantial AI revenue visibility with record backlogs.

items.title: MKC Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Margin Gains and Mexico Growth
items.summary: McCormick & Company delivered solid Q3 fiscal 2026 results with net sales rising 17.4% to $2,024.8 million, driven by the McCormick de Mexico acquisition and 1.9% organic growth. Adjusted earnings of 86 cents per share beat consensus estimates, while adjusted gross margin expanded 180 basis points to 39.3%. The company reaffirmed its fiscal 2026 outlook but expects higher commodity and freight costs in Q4, with a packaging constraint potentially reducing full-year organic growth by 30 basis points.

items.title: Can Corning's AT&T Deal Boost Its Optical Communications Growth?
items.summary: Corning Incorporated has secured a multi-year agreement worth over $3 billion with AT&T to supply fiber and cable for U.S. broadband expansion. The company is also expanding domestic production capacity and partnering with Verizon for fiber solutions. Rising data consumption and AI adoption are driving demand for advanced connectivity infrastructure.

items.title: Can Hormel Foods' Brakebush Deal Accelerate Foodservice Growth?
items.summary: Hormel Foods has agreed to acquire Brakebush Brothers, a leading value-added chicken company, for approximately $1.055 billion. The deal, expected to close in Q1 fiscal 2027, will expand Hormel's presence in value-added chicken and strengthen its Foodservice segment. Brakebush generated $1.2 billion in net sales over the past 12 months and brings established sales capabilities, customer relationships, and production scale. The acquisition is expected to support growth and unlock operational synergies, with accretion to adjusted earnings per share beginning in fiscal 2028.

items.title: ASML vs. SK Hynix: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: ASML and SK Hynix are compared as semiconductor infrastructure investments. ASML dominates lithography equipment with consistent growth (15.6% revenue growth, 29% net margin) and lower valuation risk, while SK Hynix leads in memory chips with stronger recent recovery (47% revenue growth, 44% net margin) but higher cyclical volatility. ASML is recommended for long-term 10-year investing, while SK Hynix may offer higher short-term returns with greater risk.

items.title: Even If Costco Doesn't Pay a $10 or $15 Special Dividend in 2027, I'd Still Buy the Stock
items.summary: Costco is a compelling long-term investment regardless of whether it pays a special dividend in 2027. The warehouse retailer demonstrates strong fundamentals including nearly 90% membership renewal rates, growing customer base (84.1 million paid members), expanding store count (939 stores in fiscal 2026, targeting 967 in fiscal 2027), and a loyal customer base driven by bulk pricing and private-label Kirkland Signature brand. With $20.2 billion in cash on hand, a special dividend remains possible but is not necessary to justify ownership.

items.title: Can Quanta's Electric Business Drive Further Margin Expansion?
items.summary: Quanta Services (PWR) reported a 43.6% increase in Electric revenues and 62.5% jump in operating income in Q2, with operating margins expanding 140 basis points to 11.5%. The company expects further margin improvement in the second half driven by increased transmission work and higher resource utilization. PWR stock has gained 52.5% year-to-date and currently holds a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) rating.

items.title: MU Q4 Earnings Call Points to Tighter Supply and Higher Investment
items.summary: Micron Technology reported better-than-expected Q4 FY2026 earnings with $54.23B in revenue and $33.42 non-GAAP EPS. Management expects supply constraints in DRAM and NAND markets through calendar 2028, with 26 strategic customer agreements covering 35% of revenues through 2030. The company is increasing capital expenditures to $25B in H1 FY2027 to expand capacity, and guides FY1 Q1 2027 revenues of $61.5B with 86.25% gross margin.

items.title: JBL Q4 Earnings Call Highlights AI-Led Fiscal 2027 Growth
items.summary: Jabil Inc. (JBL) reported strong Q4 earnings and provided fiscal 2027 guidance expecting revenues of $44.5B (up 24%) with AI-related revenues reaching $22.1B (54% growth). The company is expanding capacity by 4 million square feet to support over $8B in incremental revenues, while maintaining its asset-light model with capital expenditures between 1.5-2% of revenues. Management expects six Intelligent Infrastructure customers to each generate over $1B in fiscal 2027.

items.title: Intel Surges 222% in a Year: Should Investors Join the Bandwagon?
items.summary: Intel has surged 222.3% over the past year driven by AI products and improved manufacturing execution, with earnings estimates rising significantly. However, the company faces headwinds from margin compression due to higher production costs, competitive pricing pressure, and reduced China revenues as Beijing accelerates efforts to replace U.S. chips with domestic alternatives. The stock holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Not Intel. Not Nvidia. These 2 Chip Stocks Maintain an Unbreachable Moat in Advanced Chip Tech.
items.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) and ASML are identified as having unbreachable competitive moats in advanced chip technology. TSMC dominates chip fabrication with 72.5% of global foundry revenue and serves nearly all AI chip designers, while ASML holds a technological monopoly on extreme ultraviolet lithography machines essential for chip manufacturing. The article recommends both as superior long-term investments compared to Intel and Nvidia, with TSMC being the slightly better value at current prices.

items.title: Here's How Much a $1000 Investment in Fortinet Made 10 Years Ago Would Be Worth Today
items.summary: A $1,000 investment in Fortinet (FTNT) made in October 2016 would be worth $24,202.55 as of October 1, 2026, representing a 2,320% gain. This significantly outperforms the S&P 500's 252.89% return over the same period. Fortinet, a cybersecurity leader, reported strong 2Q'26 results with 26% revenue growth and raised full-year 2026 guidance to $8.02-$8.18 billion. However, the company faces competitive pressures and macroeconomic headwinds.

items.title: Buy 3 AI-Powered Momentum Stocks for October After a Mixed September
items.summary: Three AI infrastructure companies—Dell Technologies, Quanta Services, and Forgent Power Solutions—are positioned for continued momentum in October following strong September performance. Dell reported 53% revenue growth with AI server revenue doubling to $16.4 billion and a $95 billion backlog. Quanta Services' backlog surged 49% year-over-year to $53.4 billion driven by AI data center demand. Forgent Power Solutions posted record bookings of $1.5 billion and a 3.3X book-to-bill ratio, with new AI lab and hyperscaler wins.

items.title: The Median Utility Bill is $363 a Month. Here's How Much You'd Need in NextEra Energy Stock to Cover It Every Month.
items.summary: U.S. households pay a median of $363 monthly ($4,356 annually) in utility bills, rising faster than inflation. An investor would need approximately 2,058 shares of NextEra Energy (worth ~$156,500) to generate enough dividend income to cover these costs after taxes. While NextEra has a 32-year dividend growth track record averaging 10%, management has guided for slower 6% growth going forward, and the pending Dominion Energy merger creates uncertainty.

items.title: Warren Buffett's Successor, Greg Abel, Jettisoned Amazon Earlier This Year and More Than 6X'd Berkshire's Stake in the "Apple" of His Eye
items.summary: Greg Abel, Warren Buffett's successor as Berkshire Hathaway CEO, has significantly reshuffled the company's $358 billion investment portfolio. Abel sold off Amazon stock in Q1 2026, likely due to profit-taking and the departure of investment manager Todd Combs. Meanwhile, Abel has dramatically increased Berkshire's stake in Alphabet (Google parent) from $5.59 billion to $36.37 billion between December 2025 and September 2026, a 550% increase, citing the company's dominant search market position, YouTube strength, and promising AI ambitions in Google Cloud.

items.summary: ServiceNow is positioned as a major beneficiary of enterprise AI growth, with 90% of Fortune 500 companies as customers and partnerships with Nvidia, Microsoft, and Amazon. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated the market has undervalued ServiceNow, calling it 'destined to be the best platform' for enterprise AI.

items.title: Shopify vs. DoorDash: Which E-Commerce Stock Has an Edge Now?
items.summary: Shopify and DoorDash are compared as major e-commerce players. Shopify shows stronger growth with 34% revenue increase and 32% GMV growth, benefiting from merchant adoption, international expansion, and AI-driven commerce. DoorDash demonstrates solid performance with 36% revenue growth and expanding marketplace services, but faces intense competition and execution risks. Shopify is favored for greater upside potential due to its diversified ecosystem and enterprise adoption, while both stocks carry a Hold rating.

items.title: CFTC Approval Expands Coinbase's U.S. Derivatives Opportunity
items.summary: Coinbase Global has received CFTC approval for Coinbase Clearing LLC, enabling it to clear fully collateralized futures, options on futures, and swaps. This vertical integration allows the company to reduce third-party reliance, simplify operations, and accelerate new product launches. The approval strengthens Coinbase's position as a comprehensive financial infrastructure provider with native USDC collateral and 24/7 settlement capabilities.

items.title: SoundHound Adds 3 Restaurant Chains: Can Its QSR Footprint Expand?
items.summary: SoundHound AI (SOUN) is expanding its presence in quick-service restaurants with three major U.S. chain signings and 100% renewal rates among key accounts. The company reported 45% year-over-year revenue growth to $61.9 million in Q2 2026, with a major pizza chain deploying technology in over 75% of locations. However, SOUN faces competitive pressure from Toast and PAR Technology, and shares have declined 41.4% year-to-date.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Alibaba Group Holding Limited Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Alibaba Group Holding Limited alleging that the company made materially false and misleading statements regarding its business operations. The complaint claims Alibaba failed to disclose its control or affiliation with the MIIT (a Chinese military entity under the NDAA), ongoing distillation attacks against third-party AI models, and other material adverse facts. Investors who purchased Alibaba securities between June 26, 2025 and June 24, 2026 are encouraged to join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of October 5, 2026.

items.title: Alibaba's AI Spending Ramps Up: Is the Investment Paying Off?
items.summary: Alibaba is aggressively investing in AI infrastructure with June-quarter CapEx up 75% to RMB67.7B, driving a three-year RMB380B investment plan. While AI Cloud revenues grew 45% and adjusted EBITA jumped 133%, the company faces near-term pressure with free cash flow turning negative at RMB44.7B outflow and net income declining 75%. Alibaba expects AI-related CapEx to break even in roughly three years. The company competes with Microsoft and Alphabet, who are similarly scaling AI infrastructure spending.

items.title: Can Royal Caribbean's Fuel Hedges Cushion Its $1.3B Expense Outlook?
items.summary: Royal Caribbean has hedged 58% of its remaining 2026 fuel consumption at below-market rates to manage its $1.34 billion fuel expense outlook. Despite hedging efforts, second-quarter fuel costs rose to $355 million from $279 million due to higher per-metric-ton rates. The company extended hedge coverage to 49% for 2027, 29% for 2028, and 14% for 2029. Unit cruise costs are expected to increase 1.4% in 2026 including fuel, though net cruise costs excluding fuel should remain flat.

items.title: TSMC (TSM) is a Great Momentum Stock: Should You Buy?
items.summary: TSMC (TSM) receives a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating with a Momentum Style Score of B. The semiconductor company shows strong price performance, up 3.67% weekly and 63.61% annually, outpacing the S&P 500. Recent earnings estimate revisions have moved upward, with consensus estimates increasing from $16.45 to $16.56 over the past 60 days, supporting its positive momentum outlook.

items.title: Hims & Hers Health (HIMS) Investors with Substantial Losses Have Opportunity to Lead Hims & Hers Class Action Lawsuit—HBSS
items.summary: Hims & Hers Health (HIMS) faces a securities class action lawsuit following an FTC complaint alleging the company shared consumers' health data with third-party advertisers like Meta and Snap, charged for prescriptions before medical consultations, and violated ROSCA regulations. The stock dropped 14.7% on July 29, 2026, erasing over $970 million in market value. Investors with substantial losses are encouraged to participate in the class action.

items.title: Why Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) is a Great Dividend Stock Right Now
items.summary: Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) is highlighted as a compelling dividend investment opportunity for income investors. The company currently offers a 2% dividend yield with an annualized dividend of $5.36, up 4.3% year-over-year. With a conservative 49% payout ratio and expected earnings growth of 7.60% in 2026, JNJ demonstrates solid fundamentals. However, the stock carries a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold), suggesting a neutral outlook despite its strong dividend credentials.

items.title: JPMorgan Trades Below 50-Day SMA: Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
items.summary: JPMorgan (JPM) is trading below its 50-day simple moving average, signaling near-term technical weakness, though fundamental support remains solid. The bank expects 2026 net interest income of $105.5 billion supported by 10% loan growth and 7% deposit growth. Strong capital position enables a $50 billion buyback program and 10% dividend increase to $1.65 per share. items.summary: Gray Media (GTN) is presented as a superior value opportunity compared to Netflix (NFLX). GTN has a Zacks Rank of #1 (Strong Buy) with a forward P/E of 1.96 and Value grade of A, while NFLX has a Zacks Rank of #4 (Sell) with a forward P/E of 19.57 and Value grade of D. items.summary: A comparison of two aerospace-defense stocks reveals that Huntington Ingalls (HII) presents a more attractive value opportunity than Safran SA (SAFRY). items.summary: A comparison of 8x8 (EGHT) and Autodesk (ADSK) reveals that 8x8 presents a better value opportunity. 8x8 has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) with a forward P/E of 6.11 and Value grade of A, while Autodesk holds a Rank of #3 (Hold) with a forward P/E of 16.08 and Value grade of C. 8x8's lower valuation metrics and improving earnings outlook make it the superior value choice.

items.summary: A comparison of two Financial - Miscellaneous Services sector stocks reveals that Virtu Financial (VIRT) presents a better value opportunity than American Express (AXP). items.title: Nokia Oyj vs. AT&T: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares Nokia Oyj and AT&T as investment options in 2026. AT&T offers better current valuations, higher profitability margins (21.2% operating margin), and a strong 4.5% dividend yield, but carries significant net debt of $146 billion. Nokia trades at a premium valuation (26.5x forward P/E) with lower profitability (11.1% operating margin) but has no net debt and is positioned to benefit from AI infrastructure buildout. The analysis concludes that value/income investors should favor AT&T, while growth-oriented investors should consider Nokia.

items.title: Broadcom vs. SK Hynix: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: Broadcom and SK Hynix represent two different approaches to AI infrastructure investment. Broadcom offers stable, diversified enterprise infrastructure with a 36% net margin and $26.9B free cash flow but trades at a premium 30.2x forward P/E. SK Hynix delivers explosive growth with a 44% net margin and lower 7.6x valuation, but faces cyclical memory market volatility. Aggressive investors seeking direct AI exposure may prefer SK Hynix, while conservative investors should favor Broadcom's stability.

items.title: Can Higher H2 Production Support Franco-Nevada's 2026 Guidance?
items.summary: Franco-Nevada (FNV) delivered record $1.23 billion revenues in H1 2026 with 13% year-over-year growth in gold-equivalent ounces sales. The company expects 2026 GEO sales of 510,000-570,000 ounces, tracking toward the upper half of guidance. Production is expected to accelerate in H2 2026 from multiple assets including Candelaria, Tocantinzinho, and Cobre Panamá. However, FNV trades at a premium valuation of 29.91X forward earnings versus the industry average of 12.43X and carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Red Cat's USV Mix: Could Blue Ops Accelerate Margin Gains in H2?
items.summary: Red Cat Holdings (RCAT) expects gross margins to reach ~30% by end-2026 as its Blue Ops maritime division scales production of Variant 7 uncrewed surface vessels (USVs). Blue Ops moved into mass production in Q2 2026 and could achieve profitability by year-end. However, RCAT faces intensifying competition from established players like Huntington Ingalls and Textron, with the stock down 24.9% in the past month and holding a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) rating.

items.title: CAT Steps Up Acquisitions to Expand Reach and Technology: What Next?
items.summary: Caterpillar Inc. is aggressively expanding through acquisitions to strengthen its competitive position. The company agreed to acquire John Fabick Tractor Company to expand direct presence in key U.S. markets, while also acquiring RPMGlobal and Skycatch to enhance mining technology, digitalization, and AI capabilities. CAT shares have gained 73.2% in the past year and currently hold a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) rating with expected earnings growth of 43.6% in 2026.

items.title: AMP's $5.5B Buyback Aids Shareholder Returns: Will It Be Sustainable?
items.summary: Ameriprise Financial authorized an additional $5.5 billion for share repurchases through September 2028, supported by strong excess capital and free cash flow generation. The company returned $1.9 billion to shareholders in H1 2026 and has returned approximately $25 billion over the past decade. However, competing capital investments in technology, AI, and business expansion raise questions about long-term sustainability of the buyback program.

items.title: Is T1 Energy Moving Toward Vertical Integration in Solar?
items.summary: T1 Energy is building a vertically integrated U.S. solar supply chain spanning polysilicon, wafers, cells, and modules. The company operates G1_Dallas for module production and is developing G2_Austin, a 2.1 GW solar-cell facility expected to begin production in Q1 2027. T1 acquired Evervolt's solar patents including TOPCon technology for $135 million and has secured domestic sourcing agreements with Hemlock Semiconductor and Corning. The company trades at a discount to industry peers with strong earnings growth projections.

items.title: NetApp's Keystone Sovereign Targets Europe's Regulated Data Market
items.summary: NetApp is launching Keystone Sovereign, a data sovereignty-focused storage-as-a-service offering targeting regulated customers in Germany and France, with expansion planned across Europe. Keystone revenue grew 65% in fiscal 2026 as organizations seek flexible storage consumption. NetApp also unveiled Novus, a high-performance file system for GPU data feeding, and expanded Oracle Cloud support at its INSIGHT 2026 conference. The company faces competition from Supermicro and HPE, which are capitalizing on growing AI infrastructure demand.

items.title: Realty Income Expands in Europe: Can the Region Drive More Growth?
items.summary: Realty Income established a euro-denominated joint venture with KKR to expand its European operations, which now represent 20% of annualized base rent. The company invested $396.8 million in Europe during Q2 at a 7% initial yield, representing over 30% of total investment activity. Europe offers lower borrowing costs and less competition than the U.S., supporting investment spreads.

items.title: UEC Q4 Earnings Call Highlights Production Ramp and U.S. Strategy
items.summary: Uranium Energy Corp. (UEC) reported fiscal Q4 production of 82,744 pounds, up 157% sequentially, as it expanded operations across Wyoming and Texas. The company exceeded revenue expectations at $17.05 million but posted a wider-than-expected loss. UEC is scaling capacity at Christensen Ranch, ramping up Burke Hollow operations, and advancing Ludeman development while maintaining an unhedged uranium price exposure strategy. The company declined to provide fiscal 2027 guidance due to regulatory approval timing uncertainties.

items.title: CCL Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Demand Strength, 2027 Bookings
items.summary: Carnival Corporation (CCL) reported Q3 2026 earnings that beat consensus estimates, with adjusted EPS of $1.43 vs. $1.36 expected and revenues of $8.44B vs. $8.36B. The company is about half-booked for 2027 with record occupancy and pricing above prior-year levels. CCL raised full-year constant-currency net yield growth guidance to 2.3%, up from June guidance. The company plans minimal 0.5% capacity growth in 2027 while shifting deployment toward higher-return destinations like Europe and private Caribbean islands. Management flagged Q1 2027 as different due to spring booking disruption but remains constructive on the rest of the year.

items.title: Not Chips. Not Memory. Data Center Cooling Is the Unsung AI Infrastructure Play Nobody's Watching
items.summary: Data center cooling has emerged as a critical but overlooked component of AI infrastructure. Vertiv Holdings, which provides thermal management and cooling solutions for AI data centers, is positioned to benefit from the sector's growth. The company reported 24% revenue growth and 60% EPS growth in Q2, with a $15 billion order backlog and a 2.9 book-to-bill ratio. The global data center cooling market is projected to grow at 22% CAGR through 2033, reaching $128 billion.

items.title: KAYTUS KR2166V3 beschleunigt die AIHPC-Datenverarbeitung im Petabyte-Maßstab
items.summary: KAYTUS unveiled the KR2166V3, a 2U storage server featuring over 700 TB raw capacity with a single AMD EPYC 9005 socket architecture. items.summary: Hims & Hers Health faces a securities fraud class action lawsuit after the FTC alleged the telehealth provider shared consumers' sensitive health information with third-party advertisers while claiming to maintain privacy, and deceived users about billing and cancellation practices. The stock declined 14.73% on July 29, 2026, following the FTC announcement. Investors who purchased securities between August 4, 2025 and July 29, 2026 have until November 2, 2026 to file lead plaintiff applications.

items.title: Honeywell Aerospace, Inc. Notice of November 23, 2026 Application Deadline for Class Action Lawsuit - Contact Lewis Kahn, Esq. at Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC, Before Application Deadline
items.summary: A class action securities lawsuit has been filed against Honeywell Aerospace for allegedly making materially false statements and failing to disclose material adverse facts. The lawsuit claims the company failed to disclose supplier concentration risks, supply constraints, a potential false Claims Act investigation related to cybersecurity compliance on government contracts, and that these issues would materially impact sales and profitability. Investors who purchased securities between June 29, 2026 and September 1, 2026 can join the lawsuit with an application deadline of November 23, 2026.

items.summary: CrowdStrike demonstrates stronger revenue performance with consistent quarter-over-quarter growth, reaching $1.5 billion in Q2 2026, while UiPath shows more volatile revenue patterns with concerning growth deceleration from 13% to an estimated 8% year-over-year growth in Q3 2026. items.title: Cerebras Systems vs. Nebius: What Revenue Growth Trends Reveal to Investors About These Artificial Intelligence Companies
items.summary: Nebius has dramatically outpaced Cerebras Systems in revenue growth, achieving a 3x revenue advantage over two years with Q2 2026 sales of $582.3 million (454% year-over-year increase).
